name: Berkshire Taconic Community Foundation: Berkshire Environmental Endowment Fund (BEE)
summary: Annual grants for projects on water quality and related land issues in Berkshire County, Massachusetts (Housatonic and Hoosic watersheds, wetlands, bogs and fens). Nonprofits and other civic entities apply, with a 1:1 match.

fiscal_sponsor.note: For unincorporated community groups, through another nonprofit

steps: Fund advisory committee review, followed by foundation board review

eligibility.rule: Unincorporated community groups apply through another nonprofit as fiscal agent
Does not discriminate against a person or group on listed grounds
Project focuses on water quality and related land issues
Has not submitted the same proposal to another Berkshire Taconic fund

applicant_types.quote: Berkshire County nonprofit organizations, public agencies, schools or civic community entities for projects focused on water quality and related land issues.

geography.quote: Berkshire County nonprofit organizations, public agencies, schools or civic community entities for projects focused on water quality and related land issues.

access.quote: Click the apply button below to visit our application portal.

co_finance_required.quote: Applicants must be able to match the BEE grant 1:1 in cash or in in-kind services.

fiscal_sponsor.quote: Community groups that are not incorporated may apply using another nonprofit as a fiscal agent.

effort.quote: STEP 3: Complete our online grant application
Your grant application will be reviewed by the fund advisory committee, and the committee’s recommendations will be reviewed by BTCF's board of directors.

eligibility.quote: Community groups that are not incorporated may apply using another nonprofit as a fiscal agent.

Neither Berkshire Environmental Endowment Fund nor Berkshire Taconic Community Foundation support organizations which in their constitution, by-laws or practice, discriminate against a person or group on the basis of age, race, national origin, ethnicity, gender, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, political affiliation or religious belief.
Berkshire County nonprofit organizations, public agencies, schools or civic community entities for projects focused on water quality and related land issues.
It is not possible to submit the same proposal to multiple funds.

co_finance.quote: Applicants must be able to match the BEE grant 1:1 in cash or in in-kind services.

after_award.quote: Once the program or service funded is completed, the grant recipient must submit an assessment of the project's outcomes.
